releases.name: v0.7.5: SLICE extension preview for Pi 1.4.0, 1.3.0, 1.2.0 and 1.1.0
releases.body:
SLICE v0.7.5 supplies an ordinary extension for **unmodified official Pi 1.4.0, 1.3.0, 1.2.0 and 1.1.0**.

Install this release from npm, then restart Pi:

```sh
pi install npm:slice-pi@0.7.5
```

Start a new persistent text session and run `/compaction-doctor` to check it without calling a model. To follow later releases, install `npm:slice-pi` without a version and update only this package with `pi update --extension npm:slice-pi`. A plain `pi update` updates Pi itself. The same package is on Git as the fixed tag `extension-v0.7.5`; source tag `v0.7.5` selects the development monorepo, not the package:

```sh
pi install git:github.com/youxi-huang/slice@extension-v0.7.5
```

An installation from Git keeps working and updating through `extension-preview`. To move it to npm, run `pi remove git:github.com/youxi-huang/slice` and install from npm; sessions and settings carry over.

OpenCode and DSH get SLICE's `context_history` from npm too, with no build. For OpenCode, add the package to `plugin` in `opencode.json` and restart it:

```json
{ "plugin": ["slice-opencode@0.7.5"] }
```

For DSH, add it to a profile built on DSH's base bundle; the package enables itself there:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add slice-dsh@0.7.5
```

Before publication each package was installed by name from a loopback registry on official OpenCode 1.19.4 and 1.19.5 and DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 and 0.2.1-rc.5, where a scripted session compacted natively and read its original history back. Both are retrieval only: compaction stays the host's.

This pre-release supports manual /compact and Pi's threshold compaction after completed text turns, source-linked history retrieval and explicit disk-confirmed failure recovery. In the sessions it handles, overflow recovery still requires explicit /compact, and background cache warming is paused. Sessions it never protected and cannot check, such as ones with native checkpoints, images or another Pi version, are left to Pi without a failure marker. Other checkpoint formats, parent-history grants, attachments, concurrent writers and Windows are outside its verified scope.

Ordinary Agent retries after transient provider failures are supported, including partial-response connection drops. Existing retry-related blocks and text-only context-overflow failures can use explicit /compact recovery when sufficient completed source history exists. Arbitrary context edits and unfinished tool-call omissions remain unsupported.

Optional preparation has two arms, both **disabled by default**: A prepares with the configured writer; B merges data-only work notes from the session model. A validated candidate can commit its covered prefix without a writer call while every later original stays verbatim. B carries covered user messages in full and falls back to the configured writer when they do not fit. Every writer call is journaled, including cancelled or discarded preparation and unknown usage. These are experimental paths; real-provider pause, total cost, cache behavior and recovery benefits remain unproven.

Validation: this publication run passed 150 stock-Pi package and lifecycle checks on official Pi 1.4.0, 1.3.0, 1.2.0 and 1.1.0 and the full default-settings scenario suite on Pi 1.4.0 with **strict acceptance and no performance exceptions or known gaps**. Scenario evidence is bound to this exact package and source commit; the 50 ms request-overhead target and checkpoint-growth bound are required checks. Focused, security and frozen evaluator checks also remain required on final main. Services are synthetic and loopback only; no real-provider quality, latency or interactive TUI claim is made.

Source commit: dcdb2702889e78f05ef6ba7c3052a433721ff6da. Preview runtime: `stock-preview+src.b0f389ab614f8cf3`. Resident runtime keeps its v0.3.0 fingerprint.

[Usage and recovery](https://github.com/youxi-huang/slice/blob/v0.7.5/docs/context-memory/extension-preview.md) · [Validation](https://github.com/youxi-huang/slice/blob/v0.7.5/docs

### Changes
v0.6.0 is the footprint milestone's offline delivery, in the independent preview only. Three opt-in mechanisms ship behind their own switches, every one off by default: deterministic reversible reductions (`previewReduction`) replace consumed and superseded tool results in the request's projection with one line each while the session file stays untouched; labelled historical excerpts (`previewExcerpts`) answer an identifier the prompt names from compacted entries without touching the cached prefix; and derived summary renderings (`previewRendering`) fold repeated lineage and old failed paths while the stored checkpoint bytes never change.
